video_title: Trade for Kyrie? Giannis? | The Jon Krawczynski Show

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: Jon Krawczynski defends the Karl-Anthony Towns trade due to the changing financial landscape
quotes.excerpt: I can guarantee you two things: first and foremost is a lot of the people... were so happy when they traded KAT
quotes.quote: I think that that's probably the reflex reaction to from a lot of Timberwolves fans right now is, you know, and I've seen it in my social media mentions about, you know, we never should have traded KAT, never should have done, you know, this was this was terrible. And I can guarantee you two things: first and foremost is a lot of the people, and I called out one or two of them already, who are in my mentions saying we never should have traded KAT were so happy when they traded KAT right after the Dallas series and and, you know, they were putting all of the blame on him and and just ready to be done with nine years of Karl-Anthony Towns. And so I don't think that's the overwhelming sentiment among Timberwolves fans, but there certainly was a healthy contingent of Timberwolves followers out there who were ready to see something else.

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: Jon Krawczynski explains the Karl-Anthony Towns trade was a financial necessity for the Timberwolves
quotes.excerpt: The Wolves were making a deal that had to be done because the financial landscape of the league changed
quotes.quote: The Wolves were making a deal that had to be done because the financial landscape of the league changed right after they made the trade for Rudy Gobert. They brought in another big salary in Gobert, and then literally, you know, within several months after that, there was a whole new collective bargaining agreement, a whole new set of financial parameters that really changed the way that teams operate. And I think that the Timberwolves were penalized quicker than most teams, but other teams are going to go through and have gone through the same problems and the same choices that the Wolves are going through. And so, in the moment, they had to make a financial decision so that they could operate with some sort of freedom to build a team around Anthony Edwards. And they ended up getting a player that helped them get to the Western Conference Finals two years ago, did not play well this year. Donte DiVincenzo was invaluable for this team this year and probably would have helped make that series against San Antonio much more competitive if he was out there and he just was not available. And then there's people that are really high on Ousmane Dieng, and so I think he can absolutely turn into a starting player in this league.

quotes.speaker: Jim Souhan
quotes.summary_phrase: Jim Souhan highlights the New York Knicks' easy path to the NBA Finals
quotes.excerpt: What a gift to only have to beat the Cleveland Cavaliers to get to the NBA Finals. What a freaking gift.
quotes.quote: What a gift to only have to beat the Cleveland Cavaliers to get to the NBA Finals. What a freaking gift. This is, I mean, it was like varsity versus JV. And the Knicks are really good and they played really well and Towns was incredibly efficient, had a great Game 4. So I'm not I'm not dismissing the Knicks. I'm just saying, my God, that was not a finals conference finals team they played against.

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: Jon Krawczynski sees Kyrie Irving as a more reasonable trade option than Giannis Antetokounmpo
quotes.excerpt: I do think that Kyrie is a little more reasonable of an option than say Giannis is.
quotes.quote: I think that when you look at some of the deals that conceptually could be available going into this summer, we talk about Giannis Antetokounmpo, you can talk about Kyrie, you talk about a bunch of names that are going to be bandied about. I do think that Kyrie is a little more reasonable of an option than say Giannis is. And so, when you're trying to put together Giannis packages, he just makes so much money, it would have to deplete so much of your depth on your team and on your roster that you just look at it and say, man, is this really feasible, is this really a good idea? I do think that the Timberwolves will continue to explore that. I think that they will look at all sorts of different scenarios, including Giannis, but if I'm trying to look at an impactful move that could come at a price that feels like you wouldn't have to liquidate your entire roster, I think Kyrie Irving makes a lot of sense. If at the end of the day, the Wolves are not able to go get Giannis Antetokounmpo and they end up going with Kyrie Irving, I think that is a very intriguing option for them to really change the look of their roster going into next season.

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: Jon Krawczynski believes Kyrie Irving has matured and would fit well with the Timberwolves
quotes.excerpt: I really think that he was a major part of those that Dallas Mavericks team that obviously beat the Wolves
quotes.quote: Kyrie certainly at a certain stage of his career, I think in Boston and in Brooklyn, brought a lot of stray voltage around him from, you know, kind of the statements that he would make and and and some of the actions on the court and and things of that nature, but I thought once he got to Dallas, it really seemed like he found a peace, you know, and he found comfort in who he is as a player, who he is as a person. And I really think that he was a major part of those that Dallas Mavericks team that obviously beat the Wolves and went to the Finals. I just think that it looked to me from a very big distance, watching him from afar, that he had really settled into who he is as a player. And so I think if you brought him into this locker room, he would really fit in. I think that he would be a good voice and a good leader and a good soldier, all of those things. And so a lot of the concerns that some people may have had about Kyrie earlier on in his career, I don't think are necessarily front and center anymore when you're evaluating a Kyrie Irving deal.

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: Jim Souhan and Jon Krawczynski discuss the Dallas Mavericks' mismanagement of Luka Dončić and Jalen Brunson
quotes.excerpt: An all-time fumble. Like because not only, you know, we we can talk about the Luka trade which was I think the worst trade in NBA history

text_blocks.speaker: Jim Souhan
text_blocks.text: Not long ago, the Dallas Mavericks had Luka Dončić and Jalen Brunson.

text_blocks.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
text_blocks.text: Yes. Unbelievable, right? Like what an an all-time fumble. Like because not only, you know, we we can talk about the Luka trade which was I think the worst trade in NBA history and maybe in all professional sports history for the return that you got for him, but they got nothing for Jalen Brunson, Jim. They let him go in free agency. There was no compensation. There was no, you know, they they did not sign him to an extension during the season to to then trade him and and get some value for him. They got absolutely nothing for Jalen Brunson. And so when you put the two things together, I mean, I just don't know that you would find a bigger fumble in the history of the league than letting two top seven, eight players in the league leave and get you almost nothing in return for them. It's it should be studied in, you know, sports management classes of like what not to do and how not to handle it. I mean, it was it's remarkable. And then, of course, they get lucky and get Cooper Flag. So, um, I don't know if they did deserve that, but that's it, yeah.

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: Jon Krawczynski predicts a softer trade market for Giannis Antetokounmpo due to recent events
quotes.excerpt: I think that Giannis's market is going to be a little softer than maybe some people expect
quotes.quote: I think that Giannis's market is going to be a little softer than, you know, than maybe some people expect, unless Oklahoma City loses to San Antonio and then just decides, all right, we're going all in, maybe that would be a a shift, a shift in the market that would really sort of drive the price up. But right now, when you look at the Giannis market, I think the Bucks are in a tough spot because everyone knows that they have to move Giannis. Like this whole sort of charade of being able to say, no, Giannis wants to stay here, we're going to make this work. It worked, you know, last year, it worked the the previous year, and and so they were trying to drive drive up the price by doing it that way. And and you could look at that and say, it's kind of genuine, why would you want to trade the best player in franchise history for for right now, but now everyone knows it's got to happen.

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: Jon Krawczynski expects the NBA to renew its emphasis on penalizing flopping this summer
quotes.excerpt: I do expect Jim that this summer the league will look at kind of renewing flopping as a point of emphasis
quotes.quote: I do expect Jim that this summer the league will look at kind of renewing flopping as a point of emphasis for the officials. Remember, there was a time not too long ago where fines would be issued for flopping, where there was a lot more attention paid to it. And for whatever reason, and I do not know why, the league kind of gravitated away from that a little bit. And it has become such a talking point on social media, and the league is very influenced by what is being discussed on social media. And so I don't know if there will be new rules put in place to target flopping, but I do think that there will be discussions within the league, within the referees that, hey, a point of emphasis going into next season is to watch this more closely, to police this, to try and remove it from the game as much as possible. There's always going to be players trying to take advantage and trying to trick referees and stuff because it is so beneficial to a team if you can pull it off, if you can get rewarded with free throws and and other things like that, that that will always be something that that players will try, but I do believe to your point, Jim, if there's technical fouls, if there are fines, if there are other things that are really levied against players, that will start to go away. They will react to it and not want to cut money out of their checks or or have technical fouls or or all of those things. That it it will be eliminated if the league decides to say we are going to punish players who do this. And they for whatever reason, and I do not know why, they have gotten away from that over the last three, four years. And now it's, you know, it's Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, it's Chet Holmgren, it's Isaiah Hartenstein, it's Lu Dort, Isaiah Joe has done it, but also you can expand it out, Jalen Brunson does it, Luka Dončić does it, Joel Embiid does it. There's just a lot of players who try to game the system. And it's a very aesthetically unpleasing part of the game and it does make fans really not like it. And so, if the league is trying to make this game more marketable to fans, reducing those kinds of theatrics, I think should be near the top of the list and I would anticipate that we do see some chatter about that this summer at the owners meetings in in Vegas in July.

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: Jon Krawczynski discusses the Timberwolves' dilemma with Donte DiVincenzo's injury and contract
quotes.excerpt: You know what he means to this team. And so there is a bit of morality that comes into play
quotes.quote: He did everything possible for this team last year, played all 82 games, was a very, very valuable portion of this roster, suffers a devastating injury, and now is going to be rehabbing for most of next season. It is just just taking away the emotion, taking away how bad it is for Donte DiVincenzo, which it is terrible, and that is first and foremost. It's also really tough for the Timberwolves because he makes like $12.5 million next year, and you're getting no production for that money that sits on your salary cap. So you could say that, yeah, you could try to trade Donte DiVincenzo as part of a bigger package for a Giannis, for someone else, and and and just kind of then, you know, you're you're off of that kind of underwater salary right now. But when you saw, you know, in Game, what was it, Game 6 against Denver in the first round when every player on the Wolves roster wore a DiVincenzo jersey to the arena, like, you know what he means to this team. And so there is a bit of morality that comes into play with a decision like this. And I don't think that the Timberwolves want to trade Donte DiVincenzo. I think they want to keep him around, they want to help him rehab. They want to get him back fully going and then maybe by towards the end of next season, he's back on the court with the Timberwolves. But if a big opportunity comes forward to really upgrade the roster and you have to include DiVincenzo, I mean, they at least have to think about that. That said, these these guys, Tim Connelly, Chris Finch, they do look at the human side of things a lot with these deals. And I do think that there is there would be an impression that if you traded him, man, that's a cold world, like what what you did. And this this can be a cold league, and so you you may have to do it, but I think that if the Wolves could avoid doing that, they probably will.
